options.text: Genetic defect located on long arm of chromosome 4
Results from an expanded CGG repeat

questions.explanation:
5 to 7% of deaths among patients with Huntington's resulted from suicide and nearly 25% of patients attempt suicide at least once. More
than half of the suicides occurred in individuals who showed early signs of the illness but who had not been diagnosed, suggesting that
suicide may occur more frequently in the early stages of the illness (Retrieved from

questions.question_text: In which of the following dementias one is likely to �nd better recognition memory than recall memory?
questions.explanation:
HIV dementia is subcortical dementia. Recognition is better than recall in subcortical dementia while both are equally impaired in cortical
dementia.

questions.question_text:
A 42-year-old man has been complaining of troublesome motor activity for the last three years. He also has symptoms of irritability, anxiety,
and low mood. He turns up an hour late for his medical appointment and shouts at the receptionist for not being punctual. What is the
diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The age along with memory problems and psychiatric symptoms in the presence of motor problems suggest Huntington's chorea.

questions.question_text: The greatest risk factor for multi-infarct dementia is
questions.explanation:
Vascular risk factors, such as type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity and dyslipidaemia often co-occur. Each of these factors has been
associated with an increased risk of dementia, but it is uncertain which factor imposes the greatest risk.At midlife, the population
attributable risk of dementia was highest for hypertension, up to 30% of cases of late-life dementia. Later in life diabetes appears to convey
the highest risk of dementia. (Kloppenborg et al., 2008)(Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about hyperhomocysteinaemia is correct?

options.text: It is a risk factor for bipolar disorder
It is a risk factor for schizophrenia
It is a risk factor for dementia
It is a risk factor for autism
It is a risk factor for depression

correct_answer.text: It is a risk factor for dementia

questions.explanation: An increased plasma homocysteine level is a strong, independent risk factor for the development of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true for late onset schizophrenia?

options.text: Response to treatment is much better than early onset schizophrenia
A strong family history is often noted
There is usually a life long history of poor social and occupational functioning
It is seen more often in females than males

correct_answer.text: It is seen more often in females than males

questions.explanation:
Late-onset schizophrenia is seen more often in females than males. Gender distribution is estimated as 4 to 9 female predominance per
male. Sensory impairments such as deafness is commonly associated. Compared to young onset schizophrenia, there is less often a strong
family history in late onset schizophrenia.

questions.question_text:
A 77-year-old man has developed Parkinson's disease. He starts sending his wife sexually abusive text messages and o�ensive comments,
which is new and out of character. Which of the following medications is most likely to have caused this?
questions.explanation:
L-dopa administration in Parkinson's disease can lead to increased levels of brain dopamine that may play a role in the development of
hypomania and manic symptoms in such patients.

questions.question_text: What is the most common behavioural change observed in patients with Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of behavioural problems is higher than expected in patients with Huntington's disease (Craufurd et al., 2001). The most
common behavioral change observed in patients with Huntington's disease is a lack of initiative followed by poor judgement, blunting of
a�ect, poor self-care, self-centeredness and in�exibility. Irritability, impulsivity and verbal outbursts are also reported ranging from 15 to
60% of cases. Ref: Craufurd D Thompson JC Snowden (2001); Behavioral change in Huntington's disease. Neuropsychiatry and behavioral
neurology; 14: 219-226

questions.question_text: De�cits on tests of attention and visuospatial ability may be especially prominent in
questions.explanation:
Although this feature may be seen in all types of dementia, neuropsychological studies imply that de�cits on tests of attention,
concentration and visuospatial dysfunction is seen more in Lewy body type of dementia

questions.question_text: A 63-year-old lady with a mixed a�ective state also su�ers from psoriasis. Which drug is most likely to worsen her skin condition?
questions.explanation: Some skin conditions such as psoriasis and acne can be aggravated by lithium therapy

questions.question_text:
A 74-year-old man presents with history of forgetfulness and some confusion at times. Which of the following factor delays the onset of
dementia in this case?

options.text: Being a smoker in adult life

questions.explanation:
Among many factors that have been studied with respect to predicting the onset of Alzheimer's, a cognitively, physically and socially active
lifestyle in late life has been hypothesized to reduce the risk for Alzheimer's disease. Longer years of formal education has been shown to
reduce the risk of conversion (MIRAGE study data). Perneczky, R et al., 'Education attenuates the e�ect of medial temporal lobe atrophy on
cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease: the MIRAGE study,' Journal of Alzheimer's Disease: JAD 17, no. 4 (2009): 855-862.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following interventions is not recommended when managing delirium in the elderly?

options.text: Reduce the e�ects of sensory impediments
Achieve optimal levels of environmental stimulation
Preferably use low dose haloperidol for patients who require drug treatment
Ensure the safety of all patients and their immediate surroundings
Preferably use benzodiazepines for patients who require drug treatment

correct_answer.text: Preferably use benzodiazepines for patients who require drug treatment

questions.explanation:
Benzodiazepines used in delirium have the disadvantage of operating as potential aggravating factors in delirium, and elderly patients are at
high risk of falls and disinhibition.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about neurotic disorders in the elderly is not true?

options.text: Non speci�c anxiety symptoms, hypochondriacal and depressive symptoms predominate
Multiple factors may contribute to new neurotic symptoms in the elderly
The estimated prevalence of neurotic disorders is between 1-10%
Males are predominantly a�ected than females
Obessional, dissociative and conversion disorders are less common

correct_answer.text: Males are predominantly a�ected than females

questions.explanation:
The estimated prevalence of neurotic disorders is between 1-10% with a female predominance. Non-speci�c anxiety symptoms,
Hypochondriacal and depressive symptoms predominate. Obsessional, phobic, Dissociative and conversion disorders are less common.
There is an increase in referrals to psychiatry due to decreased acceptance of symptoms by the elderly. Multiple factors may contribute to
new neurotic symptoms in the elderly. The most common ones are; physical illness, major life events, bereavement, social isolation,
impaired self-care and insecure personality factors.

questions.question_text:
Which one of the following neuroimaging techniques used when assessing dementia is helpful in studying white matter lesions and vascular
lesions?
questions.explanation:
MRI scan is helpful in identifying white matter lesions and vascular changes in the cortical and subcortical regions of the brain, which aids in
the di�erential diagnosis of dementia. It is also helpful in identifying lesions in the posterior fossa of the brain.

questions.question_text:
A 70-year-old man has been diagnosed with Lewy body dementia. You are starting him on rivastigmine based on your consultant's
suggestion. Which of the following side e�ect is most likely to happen?
questions.explanation:
The most frequently reported adverse events with a higher rate in patients taking rivastigmine than placebo were nausea, vomiting and
tremor.

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric side e�ect of levo-dopa among the following is
questions.explanation:
Up to 1/3rd of patients complain of psychiatric side e�ects when taking levodopa therapy. Nearly 30% of those taking levodopa complain of
nightmares and vivid dreams. This is followed by 7% with night terrors, 5% with delirium and 3% with delusional disorder.

questions.question_text: The neurotransmitters that are most often implicated in the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease are
questions.explanation:
The neurotransmitters that are most often implicated in the pathophysiological condition of Alzheimer's disease are Acetylcholine and
norepinephrine, both of which are hypothesized to be hypoactive in Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: The personality disorder that is most prevalent after 60 years of age is
questions.explanation:
A British study (Cohen, 1994) suggested that older subjects were signi�cantly less likely than younger subjects to have any PD (6.6% vs.
10.5%; OR 0.42). This di�erence was almost entirely attributable to a threefold higher prevalence of dramatic PDs (Cluster B) in the younger
cohorts. The largest di�erences were in Antisocial PD and Histrionic PD. This study found that the highest prevalence of a PD in elderly was
for Obsessive-Compulsive PD (DSM-III) at a rate of 3.3%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is contraindicated in the elderly with psychosis and cognitive impairment?
questions.explanation:
Having reviewed the literature on the use of Olanzapine and Risperidone for the behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia, the
committee on safety of medicines concluded that each was associated with at least two-fold increase in the risk of stroke and should,
therefore, be no longer used in dementia (Du� 2004)

questions.question_text:
Older people with dementia often do not tolerate drugs as well as a healthy older person.  Which of the following is contraindicated in
patients with dementia?
questions.explanation:
The chairman of the CSM concluded that risperidone and olanzapine are associated with at least a two-fold increase in the risk of stroke
and, therefore, should no longer be used in dementia (Du�, 2004). Herrmann et al. (2004), however, found no di�erence in the risk of stroke
between risperidone and olanzapine compared with typical neuroleptics used in the treatment of behavioural problems in those with
dementia (n=11400). Others have subsequently commented on the potential detrimental e�ects of such a blanket ban (Mowat et al, 2004 )
(Karim and Byrne, Treatment of psychosis in elderly people | BJPsych Advances. (2005). Retrieved from
 Promazine has a relatively good side e�ect pro�le and so is suitable for the elderly. It is not
e�ective for schizophrenia (Maudsley Guidelines. 2007) Excerpted from Karim and Byrne. Treatment of psychosis in elderly people Advances
in Psychiatric Treatment (2005) 11: 286-296

questions.question_text: Compared to other subtypes, paranoid subtype of schizophrenia is more often associated with which of the following features?
questions.explanation:
Features such as poorer premorbid function, poorer psychosocial recovery, worse cognitive de�cits and earlier age of onset are associated
with hebephrenic or disorganized schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Factors associated with good prognosis in Alzheimer's disease include
questions.explanation:
Later onset, female gender, an absence of behavioural symptoms, and lack of depressive episodes suggest  better prognosis in Alzheimer's
disease.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a good prognostic factor in old age depression?

options.text: Severe life events during follow up period

questions.explanation:
Good prognostic factors include 1.Onset less than 70 years of age 2.a shorter duration of illness 3.Absence of physical illness 4.Good
previous adjustment 5.Good previous recovery.

questions.question_text: The response to antidepressants is expected to be generally poor in
questions.explanation:
Alexopoulos et al. (1997) proposed that cerebral ischaemic damage to the frontal-subcortical circuits could predispose, precipitate and
perpetuate late-onset depression. Simpson et al. studied the association between subcortical disease and antidepressant response in late-
life depression, concluding that a poor response could be expected in patients with vascular depression.

questions.question_text:
A 76-year-old woman presents to her GP upon her daughter's insistence. She exhibits features of late paraphrenia. Which of the following
types of delusions is most likely to be seen?
questions.explanation:
Late paraphrenia is the most common form of psychosis in old age. Persecutory delusions are the most common symptoms of late
paraphrenia and tend to relate to common themes such as neighbours spying. Auditory hallucinations occur in approximately 75% of cases.

questions.question_text: The most prevalent anxiety disorders among older adults is;
questions.explanation:
In people over age 65, anxiety disorders are the most prevalent psychiatric disorders, excluding the dementias. The most prevalent anxiety
disorder among older adults is phobic disorder and the least common in this age group is the panic disorder. The anxiety disorders are
more prevalent in women than in men across all age groups.

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old man admitted to a neurology unit has an unsteady gait and repeated falls. This is most likely to be associated with
questions.explanation:
Risk factors for falling in an elderly patient could be classi�ed as either intrinsic (e.g., lower extremity weakness, poor grip strength, balance
disorders, functional and cognitive impairment, visual de�cits) or extrinsic (e.g., polypharmacy (i.e., four or more prescription medications)
and environmental factors such as poor lighting, loose carpets, and lack of bathroom safety equipment). A meta-analysis that studied the
relationship of falls and medications, which included studies that examined both multiple and single risk factors, found a signi�cantly
increased risk from psychotropic medication (odds ratio (OR) 1.7), Class 1a antiarrhythmic medications (OR 1.6), digoxin (OR 1.2), and
diuretics (OR 1.1). Leipzig RM, Cumming RG, Tinetti ME. Drugs and falls in older people: A systematic review and meta-analysis: I.
Psychotropic drugs. J Am Geriatr Soc 1999;47:30-39.

questions.question_text: According to NINCD-ADRDA criteria, which of the following is NOT a criterion required to diagnose probable Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: Absence of systemic diseases or other brain diseases that could explain the cognitive changes
Cognitive de�cit is seen in more than one domain
Presence of cerebral atrophy in neuroimaging studies
No disturbance in level of consciousness

correct_answer.text: Presence of cerebral atrophy in neuroimaging studies

questions.explanation:
Cognitive de�cits must be seen in 2 or more domains. The absence of loss of consciousness, presence of cerebral atrophy, an appropriate
age of onset and absence of other systemic diseases to explain cognitive de�cits support the diagnosis of probable AD.

questions.question_text: Compared with early onset depression, people with late-onset depression tend to present more often with symptoms of
questions.explanation:
Late onset depression is associated more with cognitive impairment, anhedonia, psychomotor changes (Hickie et al. 2001) and weight loss
(Janssen Et Al 2006) severe life stress (Vandenberg et al. 2001). Severe psychomotor retardation or agitation occurs in up to 30% of
depressed elderly patients. Cognitive impairment has been detected in 70% of cases. The frequency and severity of life events (physical
illness, loss of a spouse) may be greater in later life than in the general population.(Hughes Et Al 1988). Grace and O'Briens �ndings that
bereavement life events were more common in those with early onset depression suggest that older people may be better able to cope with
bereavements even though they are at increased risk of experiencing them.

questions.question_text: A 75-year-old man with Parkinson's disease develops psychosis unrelated to levodopa use. Choose the best antipsychotic for his treatment.
questions.explanation:
Eight open-label studies have assessed quetiapine use in 191 patients with psychosis and Parkinson's disease, with improvement in
psychosis recorded in 152 (80%). In addition to the open-label studies, there have been two single-blind, randomized trials comparing
quetiapine and clozapine. These studies suggest that quetiapine has similar e�cacy to clozapine in controlling psychosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best indicates the status of estrogen treatment in postmenopausal women with Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: RCTs �nd no improvement in the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores
No RCTs have been conducted to examine the e�ects of estrogen in this clinical group
RCTs consistently show bene�cial e�ects on activities of daily living
RCTs �nd an improvement in MMSE scores that is sustained for at least one year
RCTs �nd small short-term improvements in MMSE scores that do not translate to clinical bene�t

correct_answer.text: RCTs �nd small short-term improvements in MMSE scores that do not translate to clinical bene�t

questions.explanation:
A Cochrane systematic review identi�ed �ve RCTs that included 210 postmenopausal women with Alzheimer disease. "The reviewers looked
at various outcomes (such as MMSE, memory, concentration, and cognitive function) after treatment with di�erent types of estrogen, at
di�erent doses, delivered by di�erent routes and for di�erent durations. Meta-analyses showed that there was a limited positive e�ect from
low-dose conjugated equine estrogens (0.625 mg once a day) but not from a higher dose (1.25 mg of conjugated equine estrogens once a
day) on the MMSE after two months, but the e�ect disappeared after three, six, and 12 months of treatment. This e�ect was small and not
clinically relevant". (

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a neurobiological feature of normal ageing process?

options.text: Loss of nerve cells in the hippocampus
Reduction in the weight of the brain
Reduction in cerebral blood �ow in the frontal lobe

questions.explanation:
There is a reduction in the weight and volume of the brain by 5% between ages 30 and 70, by 10% by the age of 80, and by 20% by the age of
90. There is a loss of nerve cells in the cortex, hippocampus, substantia nigra and Purkinje cells of the cerebellum. There may also be a
reduction in the dendritic processes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements concerning pharmacokinetics in the elderly is true?

options.text: Renal blood �ow reduces with age even in those with normal physical health
Total gastrointestinal drug absorption is reduced in the elderly
25% of adult renal function is lost by 80 years
Serum creatinine measurement is the most accurate way of measuring renal function

correct_answer.text: Renal blood �ow reduces with age even in those with normal physical health

questions.explanation:
Though GI absorption becomes slower, it does not get reduced quantitatively. Creatinine measurements can yield spurious results; hence
GFR formulas must be used to correct for age and other variables. Gastric pH increases with age (less acidic). Nearly 40% renal function is
lost by the age 80. The average decline is around 10mL/min/1.73m2 per decade after age 30. This takes an adult GFR from
130mL/min/1.73m2 to a value of 80mL/min/1.73m2 when the age is 80 (The Baltimore Longitudinal Study). Kidney mass has been reported
to be substantially reduced in old age, by approximately 20 to 25% between the age of 30 and 80 years. Renal blood �ow reduces with age
even in those with normal health. Renal blood �ow decreases by about 10% per decade after the age of 20. By age 80, RBF may be
600ml/min as compared to 1200ml/min in young adults. Schrier, RW. Diseases of the Kidney and Urinary Tract: Clinicopathologic
Foundations of Medicine. Lippincott-Wilkins, 2007 Pg 301

questions.question_text:
A70 year old lady has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's dementia recently. What is the risk of same illness for her sister provided there is no
other family history of Alzheimer's dementia?

options.text: Risk will be three times higher

correct_answer.text: Risk will be three times higher

questions.explanation:
The actual predicted risk of developing Alzheimer's disease in the �rst-degree relatives of probands with Alzheimer's disease is 15-19%,
compared with 5% in controls. Thus, the risk to the �rst-degree relatives of patients with Alzheimer's disease who developed the disorder at
any time up to the age of 85 years is increased some 3 - 4 times relative to the risk in controls. This would seem to translate to a risk of
developing Alzheimer's disease of between one in �ve and one in six. Liddell et al. (2001) Genetic risk of Alzheimer's disease: advising
relatives. The British Journal of Psychiatry, 178, 7-11.

questions.question_text:
You are seeing a 77-year-old man with late onset psychosis. He has a history of falls due to postural hypotension. Which drug is most likely
to cause orthostatic hypotension?
questions.explanation:
Risperidone and Clozapine are two drugs, which have a greater risk of causing severe postural hypotension. The suggested drugs are
amisulpride, aripiprazole, haloperidol and sulpiride.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following antidementia drugs produces signi�cant improvements in delusions and hallucinations seen in patients with Lewy
Body dementia?
questions.explanation:
A large multicenter, double-blind trial comparing Rivastigmine with placebo in patients with LBD showed signi�cant improvements in
delusions and hallucinations (Mc Keith et al. 2000). Cholinesterase inhibitors are not yet licensed for the treatment of LBD in UK but
substantial provisional evidence suggest that ACHEIs are e�ective in some LBD cases for improvement in cognitive functions and also in
treating neuropsychiatric features such as apathy, agitation and psychosis.

questions.question_text:
A 70-year-old gentleman su�ers from Parkinson's disease and is also currently depressed. His wife says he has been sending her sexually
explicit texts and also accused her of having an a�air. This is a new type of behaviour and is out of keeping with his previous pattern of
behaviour when depressed. Which drug is most likely to account for this presentation?
questions.explanation:
Ropinirole can be used by itself or in conjunction with levodopa to treat Parkinson's disease, and is particularly useful in people for whom
levodopa alone is no longer providing adequate control of symptom. Ropinirole works by stimulating these same receptor sites. This
produces the same e�ects as dopamine and acts as a dopamine substitute. Increased sex drive (libido) and excessive interest or
involvement in sexual activity (hypersexuality) is uncommon but possible side e�ect of this medication (Retrieved from

questions.question_text:
An elderly lady reports smelling of gas passed through the walls and thought her neighbours are trying to poison her. She has contacted the
police on a number of occasions over last 3 months claiming that neighbours are spying on her. The most likely diagnosis is;
questions.explanation:
Late-onset schizophrenia is characterized by paranoid delusions and hallucinations. The patients usually complain of partition delusions as
described above and may harbour persecutory delusions against neighbours. Social isolation and sensory deprivation are signi�cant
contributory factors for psychosis in the elderly. Confusingly, ICD-10 includes paraphrenia along with paranoid schizophrenia, and also
includes the term paraphrenia with delusional disorders. In the presence of hallucinations, schizophrenia is the most appropriate diagnosis.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a recognized neuroimaging �nding in late-onset depression?

options.text: Reduction in the volume of the caudate nucleus
Reduction in grey matter volume in frontal and temporal lobes

questions.explanation: Ventricles appear enlarged, not shrunk, in geriatric depression.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about learning and memory in the elderly is not true?

options.text: The elderly take longer than young persons to learn new material
IQ remains stable until approximately 70 years of age
Complete learning of new materials still occurs

questions.explanation:
Cognitive pro�le changes distinctly with the age of an individual. IQ peaks at 25 years, plateaus until 60-70 and then declines. Simple recall
becomes di�cult, and memory encoding ability diminishes. Although the elderly take longer than younger persons to learn new material,
complete learning of new material still occurs. Working memory shows a gradual decline in capacity and it is worse with increased
complexity of tasks and increased memory load. Long-term memory declines. However, remote events of personal signi�cance may be
recalled with great clarity. Older people also maintain their verbal abilities, and there is a possible drop in verbal IQ, performance IQ and
problem-solving abilities after the age of 80.

questions.question_text: Which classes of antidepressants are used as �rst-line treatments for late-onset depression?
questions.explanation:
SSRIs are often used as the �rst line treatment for late-onset depression due to their lower propensity to cause side e�ects and relative
safety in overdose.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a type of prion disease?
questions.explanation:
Prion protein is a normal brain protein, whose function is unknown. Prion related diseases occur when the protein undergoes changes,
which renders it insoluble. The diseases caused by prions are spongiform encephalopathies, which are transmissible dementias. There are
four forms of the disease in humans, all of which are rare. These are; 1. Kuru 2. Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease 3.Fatal familial insomnia 4.
Gerstmann Straussler syndrome

questions.question_text: An important feature di�erentiating vascular dementia from Alzheimer's disease is
questions.explanation:
The Hachinski Ischaemic Score (HIS) "represents a brief clinical tool helpful in the "bedside" di�erentiation of the commonest dementia
types, Dementia of Alzheimer's Type (DAT) and Vascular Dementia (VaD). It's utility has been validated by meta-analysis in pathologically
veri�ed patients with dementia. A cut-o� score = 4 for DAT and = 7 for VaD has a sensitivity of 89% and a speci�city of 89% (Moroney 1997).
It is not useful in determinations between mixed dementia and other dementia types. HIS items distinguishing VaD from DAT were stepwise
deterioration (odds ratio (OR), 6.06), �uctuating course (OR, 7.60), hypertension (OR, 4.30), history of stroke (OR, 4.30) and focal neurological

questions.question_text: The type of dementia seen in patients with Parkinson's disease is
questions.explanation: Subcortical pattern of dementia is seen in Parkinson's disease dementia.

questions.question_text: Features suggestive of pseudodementia include all except

options.text: There is often a past history of depression or an identi�able precipitant
The patients often complain about poor memory
Assessment of cognitive function often results in "Don't Know" answers

questions.explanation:
With respect to pseudodementia, the onset can be dated with some precision while symptoms are of shorter duration before medical help
is sought. There may be a more rapid progression of symptoms after onset than seen with organic dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true with regard to the pharmacokinetics of psychotropics in the elderly?

options.text: The volume of distribution of fat soluble drugs is reduced
By the age of 80, nearly 25% of renal function is lost
The rate of absorption of drugs is slower
Serum creatinine accurately re�ects renal function
The amount of drug absorbed after oral intake is reduced

correct_answer.text: The rate of absorption of drugs is slower

questions.explanation:
The rate of absorption is slower but nearly equal absorption of oral administered drugs. Absorption is not greatly a�ected. GI blood �ow is
diminished. Gastric pH is increased as acidity drops. Decreases in renal blood �ow have been approximated at 10% per decade beginning
after the fourth decade - leads to reduced creatinine clearance and GFR. A larger volume of distribution and longer half-life of lipophilic
chemicals noted because of their increased sequestration in fat e.g.; Benzodiazepines are excreted more slowly in elderly.

questions.question_text: Picks disease is characterised by all except

options.text: There is positive family history in 50% of cases
It is caused by Autosomal dominant mutation in the Tau gene (chromosome 17) with complete penetration
There is prominent atrophy of the white matter with relative sparing of the grey matter
Knife blade atrophy on CT/MRI scan is commonly seen in most cases
The onset is usually between 45-65 years

correct_answer.text: There is prominent atrophy of the white matter with relative sparing of the grey matter

questions.explanation:
In Pick's Disease, CT/MRI brain reveals bilateral symmetrical abnormalities of the frontal and temporal lobes. A milder generalised atrophy
but a marked atrophy of frontal and temporal lobes with sparing of the posterior third of the superior temporal gyrus produces the so-
called called Knife blade atrophy. Both grey and white matter is equally a�ected with blurring of the boundary.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features is not related to the biological changes seen with normal aging process?

options.text: Progressive hearing loss particularly at the high frequencies
Decrease in cardiac output and stroke volume

questions.explanation:
Changes in bodily function during old age includes a decrease in cardiac output and stroke volume, a decrease in glomerular �ltration rate, a
reduction in cerebral blood �ow and oxygenation, decreased vital capacity in the lungs, decrease in melatonin, thickening of the optic lens in
association with an inability to accommodate and progressive hearing loss particularly at the high frequencies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be used as a test of executive functioning in an older person with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation:
The tower of Hanoi is frequently used in psychological research on problem solving and executive functions. It is also a test used by
neuropsychologists trying to evaluate frontal lobe de�cits. The tower of Hanoi is a mathematical puzzle. with three rods and a number of

questions.question_text:
Ginkgo is a popular herbal remedy for memory enhancement. Patients treated for which of the following conditions should strictly avoid
Ginkgo?

options.text: Treated for bacterial pharyngitis with amoxicillin
Treated for dental pain with ibuprofen
Treated for Paget's disease with alendronate

questions.explanation:
Ginkgolide B present in Ginkgo inhibits platelet activating factor by displacing it from its binding sites. This antiplatelet activity leads to
interaction with warfarin and may cause fatal spontaneous cerebral bleeds

questions.question_text: In dementia with Lewy bodies, visual hallucinations have been reported in;
questions.explanation:
In Lewy body dementia, at least 60 to 80% cases report visual or auditory hallucinations. Mild spontaneous extra pyramidal features (70% of
cases) is also common along with repeated unexplained falls or transient clouding or loss of consciousness and increased sensitivity to
neuroleptics (60% of cases).

questions.question_text: Hachinski score is a way of looking into risk factors for
questions.explanation:
The Hachinski Ischaemic Score (HIS) represents a brief clinical tool helpful in the "bedside" di�erentiation of the commonest dementia types,
Dementia of Alzheimer's Type (DAT) and Vascular Dememntia (VaD). It's utility has been validated by meta-analysis in pathologically veri�ed
patients with dementia. A cut-o� score = 4 for DAT and = 7 for VaD has a sensitivity of 89% and a speci�city of 89% (Moroney 1997). It is not
useful in determinations between mixed dementia and other dementia types (Moroney, J.T., Meta-analysis of the Hachinski Ischaemic Score
in pathologically veri�ed dementias. Neurology, 49, 1096 – 1105.).

questions.question_text: In Parkinson's related psychosis, hallucinations in which sensory modality is common?
questions.explanation:
Parkinson's related psychosis is mostly related to antiparkinsonian drugs. Both dopaminergic/anticholinergic medications are implicated.
Hallucinations are common, seen in 20% of cases- especially visual modality, delusions 3-30%. Low-dose (less than 100 mg/day) clozapine
can improve psychosis without worsening parkinsonism. Quetiapine can also be used.

questions.explanation: Visual hallucinations can be present in more than 80% of patients with LBD.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is classi�ed as a 'behavioural symptom' seen in Alzheimer's Dementia?
questions.explanation:
In patients with Alzheimer's, behavioural symptoms would include wandering, aggression, anger outbursts, sexual disinhibition,
incontinence, excessive eating and searching behaviour. Psychiatric symptoms include delusions (15%), auditory and visual hallucinations
(10-15%), and depression requiring treatment in 20% of patients.
